purpose: Evaluate how asymmetric false-positive and false-negative costs affect threshold selection and model choice, both without and with minimum recall constraints.
cost_function: Total Cost = (FP cost × FP) + (FN cost × FN)

analysis.part_1: Cost-sensitive threshold selection without a minimum recall constraint.
analysis.part_2: Cost-sensitive threshold selection subject to minimum recall constraints.

key_findings.cost_only: Random Forest produced the lowest total cost among the evaluated models in all four tested cost scenarios.
key_findings.threshold_behavior: For Random Forest, the cost-optimal threshold decreased from 0.35 to 0.15 as the relative false-negative cost increased from 1 to 10.
key_findings.recall_constraints: At minimum recall requirements of 80% and 90%, Random Forest was the only model with a feasible tested threshold.
key_findings.highest_tested_constraint: No evaluated model-threshold combination reached the 95% minimum recall requirement.

important_observations: Increasing the relative cost of false negatives generally favored lower decision thresholds.
Lower thresholds increased recall and reduced false negatives but increased false positives.
Increasing the minimum recall requirement reduced the number of feasible model-threshold combinations.
The cost scenarios are illustrative relative-cost scenarios and are not claimed to represent measured industrial monetary costs.
research_decision: Retain Random Forest as the strongest candidate for final model selection under the tested cost and minimum-recall scenarios. Final model and threshold selection is deferred to Experiment 6.
